issues.claim: A 0.8% label difference is plausible from this alone, but it is a hypothesis to check, not a conclusion.
issues.problem: Overstated. Float32 rounding flips a row only if its feature is within rounding error of a split or its score within rounding error of the threshold; for a continuous score that is far below 0.8% of rows. skl2onnx docs: in most cases float and double comparison gives the same result.
issues.replacement: Float32 rounding alone usually flips far fewer rows than 0.8% (it needs that share of rows to sit within rounding error of a split or of the decision threshold; the skl2onnx documentation says float and double comparisons give the same result in most cases), so treat a 0.8% difference as a sign of a real discrepancy, such as unseen-category or missing-value handling, scaler dtype, or preprocessing outside the graph, until the margin analysis shows otherwise.

issues.claim: If all 1,600 have |p - threshold| < 1e-4, the flips are numeric ties at the threshold and acceptable
issues.problem: Internally inconsistent with a realistic score distribution: it would put 0.8% of all rows within 1e-4 of the threshold (density ~40x average); possible only for quantised/tied scores.
issues.replacement: If all 1,600 have |p - threshold| < 1e-4 (unlikely for a continuous score, since it would put 0.8% of all rows within 1e-4 of the threshold; look for quantised or tied scores), the flips are numeric ties at the threshold and acceptable

evidence.evidence: SRE workbook canarying; before/after comparison is hard because time causes change.

issues.claim: Outcome check: 14 days after Stage 3 starts, compare matured chargeback and false-positive rates for the cohorts scored by old and new models, using the sticky assignment log.
issues.problem: Chargebacks arrive up to 45 days late, so nothing is matured 14 days after Stage 3 starts; also the previous model is kept warm only 7 days.
issues.replacement: Outcome check: run an interim comparison 14 days after Stage 3 starts (chargebacks are only partly matured, so compare same-age slices of the cohorts scored by the old and new models), and the final comparison of matured chargeback and false-positive rates once labels have had the full 45 days, using the sticky assignment log.

difficulty_rationale: Open-ended policy design needing statistics, delayed labels and automation boundaries.
